title: R’ Nehorai, an Amora
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Chullin 55b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.55b.16): he said in the name of Shmuel.[^2]

At the end of [Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 71](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.71.9), R-A [ר״א] and R’ Nehorai dispute which tribe Elijah was from. R’ Nehorai says he was from Gad. R’ Pilipi bar Nehorai says, ‘What leads you to say so?’ He says to him, ‘For it is written,’ etc. It appears to Hyman that it should read, ‘R’ Pilipi said to R’ Nehorai.’ Hyman cites Tanna Devei Eliyahu Rabbah, chapter 18, and Tanna Devei Eliyahu Zuta, chapter 15, saying that there Elijah told him which tribe he was from. Hyman considers it very likely that this is the R’ Nehorai found in the [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.9.2.4-5), where, in Hyman’s account, Elijah asked Rabbi Nehorai [נהוריי], ‘Why were tremors and creeping creatures created?’; and in [Ruth Rabbah 4:1 (Hyman cites the end of chapter 3)](https://www.sefaria.org/Ruth_Rabbah.4.1), where Elijah asked him [or: they asked Elijah], ‘What is this that is written, “And Shacharaim begot,”’ etc.[^1][^3]

notes.text: The linked Bereshit Rabbah reads Eliezer at the opening and Elazar later. It has Pilipi bar Nehorai where Hyman proposes “Pilipi said to Nehorai.”
Chullin names Rabbi Nehorai reporting in Shmuel’s name. The Yerushalmi has Elijah ask Nehorai about earthquakes and then about creeping creatures in separate questions.
The linked Ruth Rabbah makes Elijah the questioner in the Shacharaim passage. Hyman proposes one Nehorai across these accounts and reports additional parallels in Tanna Devei Eliyahu.
